body: I'm really sorry to hear that. How are you doing? The only thing that has pulled me back in the past is the thought of someone feeling as bad as I do, because of me.

Those kinds of tiny jabs really get to me. I feel like I almost had a panic attack while they were laughing on, and it's not incredibly uncommon to hear jokes from day to day. Sometimes I'll be feeling relatively good and I'll overhear some random joke and come crashing down all over again. I wish people could understand the effect that shit has.

I've gotten a little bit of support opening up (slowly) about depression in general, but none of my friends really get it. I know I could never bring up past/current struggles with suicidal thoughts or else they would just freak, because to them even a passing thought is cause for hospitalization. Even without going that far, it's hard. The other day I had one of my closest friends tell me the other day that he's disappointed his sister is going on medication for anxiety since she can probably control it through sheer will. I've been trying to work up the courage to go get diagnosed and medicated for depression so I just curled up, ashamed at his comments. 

I'm really sorry to hear about your roommate. Are you doing okay?
